title: Resumable checkpointed canary with traffic leases and metric anchors
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Production canaries today fail hard when a transient infra or metric anomaly triggers an automatic rollback. For stateful model swaps (session-affine routing, KV cache warmup) that leads to repeated costly warmups and poor user experience. This PR implements a resumable, checkpointed canary primitive that: (1) snapshots canary state (traffic assignment, KV cache warmups, small replay buffer) at stable points, (2) assigns time-bound traffic leases to cohorts so traffic ownership can be recovered or extended, and (3) evaluates canaries relative to metric anchors (baseline reference metrics) instead of absolute thresholds. Together these reduce unnecessary rollbacks and allow safe rewind/retry without full cold restarts.

What this PR delivers: single coherent implementation across the rollout controller and serving runtime that includes: - Checkpoint creation and storage hooks (controller side) for canary stages, with retention policy and compact delta format. - Traffic lease mechanism: tokenized lease metadata attached to cohort routes; leases are renew/evict aware and surface in the console. - Metric anchors: declarative baseline anchors you can pin per rollout (latency P95, error rate baseline, quality eval score). Anchors are used by the safety gates and reported in rollout traces. - Resume/rewind operator: when a canary fails transiently, operators can resume from a checkpoint and reassign traffic via lease transfer instead of full swap. - API + CLI additions: rollout.resume, rollout.checkpoint-list, rollout.pin-anchor. - Migration path: older rollout specs are backward compatible; new fields are optional.

Design notes (short): - Checkpoints are lightweight tar+manifest stored in internal objectstore (S3/GCS) with TTL. - Lease tokens encode cohort id, expiry, and a monotonically increasing epoch used by serving plane to avoid split-brain. - Anchors are stored as name->metric mapping; evaluation uses relative-delta scoring and a configurable conservatism factor. - Safety: resume paths require an explicit operator action (no automatic resume) unless CanaryPolicy.allow_auto_resume is set. Resume includes an idempotent verification step: recheck anchored metrics against a short shadow window before opening live traffic.

Backward compatibility and rollout rule changes: - Existing rollout specs remain valid. - New fields: .spec.checkpoints.enabled (bool), .spec.traffic.lease_ttl (duration), .spec.anchors[]. These default to safe values (checkpoints: false, lease_ttl: 0 meaning no lease, anchors: empty). - Default controller behavior unchanged until a rollout opts in.

Testing and evaluation: - Unit tests for checkpoint manifest serialization, lease token verification, anchor scoring (added ~45 new tests). - E2E canary smoke harness extended to simulated transient infra failures to validate resume reduces full cold restarts. - Local perf tests show checkpoint creation cost ~120ms for a typical model bundle snapshot, and resume path reduces warm-start latency by ~2.3x on average in our lab workloads.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked in PR) and linear tickets referenced - [x] Controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Serving runtime hook to honor lease epochs - [x] Console UI hooks (staged; feature flag gated) - [x] CLI commands for ops - [x] Migration notes and docs update - [x] Observability: rollout traces, checkpoint metrics, lease renew/expire events

Commits (high-level): - feat(controller): checkpoint manager and TTL retention - feat(serve): honor traffic lease epochs and expose lease debug endpoint - feat(ui): checkpoint/lease controls behind feature flag - feat(cli): rollout.resume and rollout.checkpoint-list - fix(tests): stabilize anchor scoring unit tests - docs: rollout spec examples and migration guide

Files changed (high-level): ["controller/pkg/checkpoint/manager.go", "controller/api/v1/rollout_types.go", "serve/lease/handler.go", "serve/lease/protocol.md", "cli/rollout_resume.go", "ui/src/components/CheckpointPanel.tsx", "docs/rollouts/checkpointing.md", "tests/e2e/canary_resume_test.go", "observability/rollout_metrics.prom", "Makefile", "go.mod", "package.json" ]

Review conversation (selected): - Evan Murthy (2026-01-18): "Can you clarify lease epoch propagation during controller failover? If two controller replicas race, how do we avoid double-assigning?" - Author reply (Aisha, 2026-01-18): "Lease tokens include epoch + monotonic lease version tied to controller leader id. Serving plane verifies epoch monotonicity and rejects lower-epoch reassignment. I added a note in serve/lease/protocol.md and an extra unit test simulating leader change." - Lina Chen (2026-01-20): "Suggest we expose checkpoint size and creation latency to the console; ops will need that when planning resume windows." - Author (2026-01-21): "Added checkpoint.size_bytes and checkpoint.create_ms metrics and wired to rollout traces." - Jordan Reyes (2026-01-24): "One CI flake on canary_resume_test.go due to a timing assumption; recommend increasing timeout with a comment." - Author (2026-01-25): "Fixed timing and annotated test to avoid future flakes. Reran CI."

CI summary: Initial run: 18 checks, 1 flaky e2e failure. Reran e2e on CI-2, final status: pass (all checks green). Build artifacts: controller image built (sha: abcdef1), serve image built (sha: abcdef2).

Merge: Squash and merge by Lina Chen on 2026-01-28. Tags created: rollout/checkpoint-v1. Feature flag: rollout.checkpoints_beta enabled for internal clusters only. Post-merge actions: docs published to internal site, scheduled rollout of UI panel in next minor release.

Notes for operators: - To opt-in: update your rollout YAML, set spec.checkpoints.enabled=true and optionally set spec.traffic.lease_ttl to a non-zero duration. - Resume is manual: use `redwood rollout resume --from-checkpoint <id> --to-cohort <cohort>` and verify anchor windows in the console before unpausing. - If you encounter lease rejection logs on serve plane, check controller leader status and lease epochs (metric: serve.lease.reject_epoch).
